warning: The signing keys in this file are test keys with publicly known values. They exist so that every signature here can be reproduced. Never use them on any network. Each named key carries a separate scalar per scheme, and no scalar signs under both: a secret key used for Schnorr and for ECDSA alike can be recovered outright from a nonce reused across the two, so the schemes are separated here as they are separated at key derivation. Do not collapse the pair back into one scalar when adapting these vectors. No valid vector names a keyType, and that is the convention rather than an omission: absent means unshielded, which is the only key type that signs messages, so a vector for the absent case would be indistinguishable from every other vector here. The one vector that names the field names the rejected value. Read an input without a keyType as asking for an unshielded key, not as leaving the key type open. Two vectors carry an unpaired surrogate escape in input.data on purpose, to check that an implementation rejects a lone surrogate instead of substituting U+FFFD; the escape is the only way to write one, a lone surrogate having no UTF-8 form. RFC 8259 section 8.2 permits it as non-interoperable, not ungrammatical: Node and Python parse this file, jq does not. Use a parser that accepts it rather than skipping the two vectors.

vectors.name: schnorr-empty-text
vectors.description: Empty text payload; the message is the prefix, a zero length and a colon.

vectors.name: schnorr-empty-hex
vectors.description: Empty hex payload; the same message as the empty text payload.

vectors.name: schnorr-empty-base64
vectors.description: Empty base64 payload; the same message again.

vectors.name: ecdsa-empty-text
vectors.description: The empty payload under ECDSA; same message and digest, different signature.

vectors.name: schnorr-hex-decade
vectors.description: The three bytes de ca de, requested as hex; the length is 3, not 6.

vectors.name: schnorr-text-decade
vectors.description: The same six characters as text: six ASCII bytes, a different message entirely.

vectors.name: schnorr-hex-decade-uppercase
vectors.description: Uppercase hex decodes to the same bytes, so it produces the same message.

vectors.name: schnorr-base64-decade
vectors.description: Base64 of those same three bytes; again the same message, so the signatures are interchangeable.

vectors.name: schnorr-hex-decade-second-key
vectors.description: The same message signed by a second key, so a verifier cannot ignore the verifying key.

vectors.name: ecdsa-hex-decade
vectors.description: Those three bytes under ECDSA; the bound value is the same digest as the BIP-340 vectors.

vectors.name: ecdsa-text-decade
vectors.description: The six-character text payload under ECDSA.

vectors.name: ecdsa-hex-decade-second-key
vectors.description: The ECDSA message signed by the second key.

vectors.name: schnorr-text-ascii
vectors.description: A plain ASCII sign-in challenge, naming the party asking and carrying a nonce, over two lines.

input.data:
example.com asks you to sign in.

Nonce: 6f2b8d1c47a903e5b8d24f6017c3ae9b

vectors.name: schnorr-text-non-ascii
vectors.description: Latin text with diacritics: 26 UTF-8 bytes over 17 characters.

vectors.name: schnorr-text-astral
vectors.description: A character outside the basic multilingual plane, encoded as one four-byte UTF-8 sequence.

vectors.name: ecdsa-text-astral
vectors.description: The same astral-plane payload under ECDSA.

vectors.name: schnorr-text-decomposed-accent
vectors.description: A decomposed accent (e + U+0301). An implementation applying NFC would sign two bytes, not three.

vectors.name: schnorr-text-payload-resembling-a-message
vectors.description: A payload that is itself a well-formed prefixed message; the structural parse must still be unique.

vectors.name: schnorr-hex-single-zero-byte
vectors.description: A one-byte payload that is NUL; the message is not NUL-terminated and is not shortened.

vectors.name: schnorr-hex-nine-bytes
vectors.description: Nine bytes: a one-digit decimal length.

vectors.name: schnorr-hex-ten-bytes
vectors.description: Ten bytes: the decimal length gains a digit, so the message gains a byte.

vectors.name: schnorr-hex-ninety-nine-bytes
vectors.description: Ninety-nine bytes: a two-digit decimal length.

vectors.name: schnorr-hex-one-hundred-bytes
vectors.description: One hundred bytes: a three-digit decimal length.

vectors.name: schnorr-hex-thirty-two-byte-challenge
vectors.description: A 32-byte challenge whose message and verifying key match a wallet-produced vector the ledger accepted; the signature differs because the wallet’s auxiliary randomness was not recorded.

vectors.name: ecdsa-hex-thirty-two-byte-challenge
vectors.description: The same 32-byte challenge under ECDSA.

vectors.name: schnorr-text-byte-order-mark
vectors.description: A leading U+FEFF is ordinary content: it is encoded as ef bb bf, never stripped, and never added.

vectors.name: ecdsa-hex-decade-odd-y-key
vectors.description: A third key whose compressed verifying key leads with 03; a verifier that assumes 02 fails only here.

vectors.name: invalid-hex-odd-length
vectors.description: Odd-length hex must be rejected, never truncated and never padded.

vectors.name: invalid-hex-zero-x-prefix
vectors.description: A 0x prefix must be rejected, not stripped.

vectors.name: invalid-hex-zero-x-prefix-uppercase
vectors.description: The uppercase 0X prefix likewise.

vectors.name: invalid-hex-whitespace
vectors.description: Whitespace inside hex must be rejected, not stripped.

vectors.name: invalid-hex-underscore
vectors.description: A digit-group separator is not part of the hex alphabet.

vectors.name: invalid-hex-out-of-alphabet
vectors.description: A character outside [0-9a-fA-F] must be rejected.

vectors.name: invalid-base64-length-one-mod-four
vectors.description: A base64 length of 1 mod 4 must be rejected; a permissive decoder invents bytes here.

vectors.name: invalid-base64-length-one-mod-four-longer
vectors.description: The same defect past the first quantum.

vectors.name: invalid-base64-unpadded
vectors.description: Padding is required: the length must be a multiple of 4.

vectors.name: invalid-base64-url-safe-alphabet
vectors.description: The URL-safe alphabet is a different encoding and must be rejected.

vectors.name: invalid-base64-line-break
vectors.description: A line-wrapped payload must be rejected, not unwrapped.

vectors.name: invalid-base64-space
vectors.description: A space inside base64 must be rejected, not stripped.

vectors.name: invalid-base64-out-of-alphabet
vectors.description: A character outside the RFC 4648 section 4 alphabet must be rejected.

vectors.name: invalid-base64-padding-inside
vectors.description: Padding may only end the final quantum.

vectors.name: invalid-base64-padding-first
vectors.description: Padding that is not final at all; a decoder that scans for = anywhere invents bytes here.

vectors.name: invalid-base64-padding-only
vectors.description: Four padding characters: more padding than a final quantum can carry, and no data at all.

vectors.name: invalid-base64-trailing-bits-two-character-quantum
vectors.description: A two-character final quantum whose four spare bits are set; YQ== is the canonical spelling of the same byte.

vectors.name: invalid-base64-trailing-bits-three-character-quantum
vectors.description: A three-character final quantum whose two spare bits are set; YWI= is the canonical spelling of the same two bytes.

vectors.name: invalid-text-unpaired-high-surrogate
vectors.description: An unpaired high surrogate must be rejected, not replaced with U+FFFD.

vectors.name: invalid-text-unpaired-low-surrogate
vectors.description: An unpaired low surrogate likewise.

vectors.name: invalid-encoding-unrecognised
vectors.description: An encoding that names none of the three must be rejected, not mapped onto the nearest one: utf8 is not text, however obvious the intent looks.

vectors.name: invalid-encoding-absent
vectors.description: No encoding at all. There is no default: a producer that sniffs the data here has three readings to choose between and no ground to choose on.

vectors.name: invalid-keytype-shielded
vectors.description: A shielded keyType must be rejected even though the payload decodes; only unshielded keys sign messages.

vectors.name: reject-signature-is-not-an-object
vectors.description: The Signature is JSON null, so there is no field to read; a verifier reaches a verdict instead of failing on the missing object.

vectors.name: reject-signature-is-a-json-array
vectors.description: A genuine Signature wrapped in a single-element JSON array, the other value typeof calls an object, and the shape a producer that batches its results returns. The container step is what refuses it: a verifier that unwraps the array accepts a Signature that never arrived as one.

vectors.name: reject-scheme-absent
vectors.description: A genuine Schnorr signature whose Signature omits scheme altogether, as a producer written before the field existed emits it. The field is required: there is no scheme to fall back to, and a verifier that supplies one accepts a signature it must refuse.

vectors.name: reject-scheme-is-null
vectors.description: A null scheme names no scheme; only the two literals do, and a verifier must not read null as a request to pick one.

vectors.name: reject-scheme-is-the-ledger-tag
vectors.description: The tag the Midnight ledger uses for the same scheme, forwarded verbatim into scheme. It is neither of the two literals the discriminator admits, so a verifier rejects it rather than mapping it.

vectors.name: reject-uppercase-wire-hex
vectors.description: Everything is genuine except that data is uppercase; the wire form is lowercase and is not case-insensitive.

vectors.name: reject-uppercase-signature
vectors.description: Everything is genuine except that signature is uppercase; the same 64 bytes either way, so nothing but the wire form refuses it. Without this the casing rule is pinned on two of the three fields and a verifier may lowercase the third.

vectors.name: reject-uppercase-verifying-key
vectors.description: Everything is genuine except that verifyingKey is uppercase; hex decodes to the same point either way, so nothing but the wire form refuses it.

vectors.name: reject-odd-length-data
vectors.description: A genuine data field with one hex character appended: a decoder that drops the trailing half byte rebuilds the message and accepts, so nothing but the even-length rule refuses it.

vectors.name: reject-odd-length-signature
vectors.description: A genuine signature field with one hex character appended: Buffer.from drops the trailing half byte, so a verifier that counts bytes after decoding sees the 64 it wants and accepts. The even-length rule is what refuses it, and it has to be pinned on signature separately because the 64-byte rule alone would let an odd count through a decode-first verifier.

vectors.name: reject-uncompressed-sec1-verifying-key
vectors.description: A real but uncompressed 65-byte SEC1 point under ECDSA; only the 33-byte compressed form is admitted.

vectors.name: reject-odd-length-verifying-key
vectors.description: A genuine verifyingKey with one hex character appended, the third and last field the even-length rule governs. As with signature, a verifier that decodes first and counts bytes afterwards drops the trailing half byte, recovers the real key and accepts.

vectors.name: reject-der-encoded-signature
vectors.description: A genuine ECDSA signature re-spelled as DER, which is what OpenSSL and libsecp256k1 emit by default: the same (r, s) over the same digest, so a verifier that hands whatever length it was given to a DER-accepting library verifies it and accepts. Only the 64-byte rule refuses it.

vectors.name: reject-x-only-key-under-ecdsa
vectors.description: The 32-byte x coordinate of a genuine ECDSA verifying key, with the SEC1 lead byte dropped: a verifier that re-adds one — the BIP-340 key shape reaching an ECDSA signature — reconstructs the real point and accepts. Only the length rule refuses it, and the uncompressed vector cannot stand in for it because that one is caught by the lead byte instead.

vectors.name: reject-stringified-signature-object
vectors.description: A tagged ledger value coerced with String(...) rather than unwrapped: well-formed enough to look like a field, never a signature.

vectors.name: reject-data-absent
vectors.description: The signed bytes are missing altogether, so there is nothing to parse or to compare against the payload.

vectors.name: reject-data-echoes-the-payload
vectors.description: data carries the payload alone with no prefix: the echo several producers ship, and a signature over a message no one can reconstruct.

vectors.name: reject-foreign-prefix
vectors.description: A genuine signature over a message built on a different 24-byte separator: the length header, the payload and the signature are all sound, so the prefix is the only thing that refuses it. Without this vector a verifier that never compares the prefix passes the whole file, and the prefix is what keeps a message signature from being read as any other signed structure.

vectors.name: reject-leading-zero-length
vectors.description: A genuinely signed message whose decimal length is zero-padded; the length has exactly one spelling.

vectors.name: reject-unterminated-length
vectors.description: A genuinely signed message whose digit run is not followed by a colon, so the payload never begins.

vectors.name: reject-declared-length-mismatch
vectors.description: A genuinely signed message declaring four bytes and carrying three; a truncating producer emits exactly this.

vectors.name: reject-payload-is-not-the-requested-payload
vectors.description: A structurally perfect, genuinely signed message over one byte the caller did not send.

vectors.name: reject-high-s-ecdsa-twin
vectors.description: The (r, n-s) twin of a genuine ECDSA signature: valid curve arithmetic, forged from the signature alone, and non-canonical.

vectors.name: reject-signature-over-a-different-message
vectors.description: Every structural check passes and the payload matches, but the signature was made over other bytes.
